messages:
Maya S.: FYI customer acme-ingest reported our JSON mode returning heterogeneous array items — their strict parser fails on ingestion.

Maya S.: Repro payload they used:
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers: {
  Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX,
  x-request-id: req_0a3f9c2b,
  content-type: application/json
}
Body: {
  \"mode\": \"json\",
  \"json_schema\": {\"type\":\"array\", \"items\": {\"type\": \"object\", \"required\": [\"id\",\"user\",\"text\"]}},
  \"temperature\": 0.2,
  \"max_tokens\": 512,
  \"seed\": 42,
  \"stream\": false,
  \"preserve_array_order\": true
}
```

Maya S.: Example raw response (truncated from their capture):
```
[
  { \"id\": \"a1\", \"user\": {\"id\": \"u1\", \"name\": \"J\"}, \"text\": \"ok\" },
  \"just-a-string-fallback\",
  { \"id\": null, \"text\": \"missing user\", \"__debug\": {\"score\":0.71} },
  { \"id\": \"a4\", \"user\": {\"name\": \"Z\"}, \"text\": \"ok\", \"extra_key\": \"v\" }
]
```

Maya S.: Client errors: \"schema mismatch: items[1] expected object but got string\" then \"required user.id missing for items[2]\". They said this started after last week\'s model rollout. Affects ~0.8% of requests for that route.

Felix H.: Which model/variant and exact request ids/timestamps? Any correlation ids from failed runs?

Maya S.: Model: redwood/gpt-infer-2.1-quant@rev-20260310; timestamp ~2026-03-11T15:23:08Z; x-request-id req_0a3f9c2b and 4 other failing req ids attached in case. They included full raw bytes.

Arjun (SE): Sounds like schema-drift + some structured-decoding relaxation in the new variant. Two modes: (1) model emits plain strings inside arrays when uncertain, (2) it emits optional internal debug keys we currently don\'t strip (e.g., __debug, __score). Also ordering: they rely on header-first ordering but model sometimes echoes header as separate item.

Emily (SRE): Can we map this to the runtime deploy? Any batching changes that could concat tokens leading to stray string items? Also saw small latency spike during that window.

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-11T15:20:00Z -> infra/runtime#v2.3.6 (rolling). 2.6% rollouts remaining. No failed healthchecks reported.

support-bot: Created escalation ES-2026-578 and linked CA-1184.

Felix H.: Devs: request reproducible minimal steps: POST the exact body with seed and temperature, set stream=false, capture raw response bytes and include x-request-id header. Please paste one full raw response and headers.

Maya S.: Done in the case. They used \"json_mode\": \"objects\" and preserve_array_order=true. No streaming.

Arjun (SE): Short-term mitigations we can push quickly:
- Pin customer to redwood/gpt-infer-2.1-quant@rev-20260301 (previous stable) for their route via routing rule.
- Server-side schema validation: if postprocessed JSON fails the provided schema, trigger 1 deterministic retry with lower temperature and penalize special tokens, then revalidate. If still failing, return an explicit failure object (text fallback + error code) so client can safely retry instead of crashing.
- Remove internal keys (\"__debug\", \"__score\", etc.) from structured outputs before returning.

Emily (SRE): Ops plan:
- If validation fail rate > 1% across customers for same model route, rollback runtime change.
- Add logging hook in structured-output pipeline: sample model_token_stream -> postprocess -> schema_validate and send truncated sample to logs. Alert if fail rate > 0.1%.
- Canary pin for 2 hours once rolled to stable.

Li (PM): High priority. Customer ingestion pipeline is blocked. Hotfix for schema-enforcement + route pinning first, then follow-up: stronger eval harness and guardrail tests.

Maya S.: Customer agreed to pin and asked for ETA. I told them 2-4 hours for pin + temporary server-side validation. They will supply more failing examples (5 attached so far).

Felix H.: Also confirm whether our structured-output decoder has an \"allow_partial_objects\" or \"tolerate_heterogeneous_array\" flag enabled for that variant. If yes, disable for this route and push canary.

Arjun (SE): I found that variant had \"allow_partial_objects: true\" in the model config to reduce strict tokenization failures. Recommend disabling for strict JSON routes. We should also prefer injecting metadata via system messages instead of embedding header tokens in the output array to avoid ordering assumptions.

Maya S.: Next actions recorded in ES-2026-578: (1) Pin customer to rev-20260301, (2) Short-term server-side schema validation + strip internal keys, (3) Add regression test that generates 10k json-mode samples to detect mixed-type arrays, (4) Follow-up postmortem if rollback required.

Emily (SRE): I\'ll add a validation metric to Grafana and watch for anomalies. Will update channel in 30m.

Maya S.: Thanks all \":thumbsup:\". Closing Slack thread once pin and validation are live and documented in the case.
